S1_incident_reporting.quote: A manufacturer must report any thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or material property damage to the competent regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a preliminary incident record. Incidents presenting an ongoing risk must be reported to affected customers and nearby occupants who may be exposed within 48 hours of awareness, with immediate protective instructions; other affected customers must be notified within 5 calendar days.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% of tested units per model. Pending confirmation, the regulator may authorize continued or limited sales subject to proportionate safeguards, monitoring, and customer notice where warranted by the evidence; it may restrict sales when necessary to address a serious risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: For units already installed when this rule takes effect, manufacturers must provide a no-cost retrofit or equivalent compliant upgrade within six years. If a unit cannot be upgraded, the manufacturer must notify its owner and regulator and provide a safe replacement or other regulator-approved mitigation.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. The suppression system must be designed and validated for the unit's battery chemistry and foreseeable operating conditions, and must not create an unreasonable risk of toxic exposure or impede emergency response.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a regulator-supervised recall when a model's thermal incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period. The manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, stop new sales, and provide repair, replacement, or refund options and safe handling instructions.

document.section_notes: The only weakened section is S2: the 5% limit has no sales stop and no time bound, so a model above 5% can keep selling under regulator authorization, which mainly protects Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%). S1 is strong (24-hour reporting covering all thermal incidents while investigations proceed), which bites on both companies' unreported incidents. S5's 8-per-100k mandatory recall trigger is at the safe level and would reach Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9), though the S4 36-month suppression delay favours Halcyon.
